candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Handling Hazardous and Infectious Materials, printed p.25 / PDF p.29: follow procedures for handling biohazardous and hazardous materials; ensure safe implementation of internal radiation therapy
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — radiation-safety principles / therapeutic radioactive material
candidate.educational_objective: Use ALARA-based radiation-safety principles when caring for clients receiving therapeutic radioactive material: minimize exposure time, maximize distance when clinically feasible, and follow source-specific shielding/containment instructions.

options.A: Minimize unnecessary exposure time, maximize distance when care permits, and use the shielding or containment measures specified for the radioactive source
options.B: Use the same precautions as for hazardous antineoplastic drugs because radioactive materials require no radiation-specific controls
options.C: Remain as close to the client as possible between care activities because distance does not affect radiation dose
options.D: Ignore the facility radiation-safety instructions once the therapeutic dose has been administered

candidate.rationale: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission identifies time, distance, shielding, and containment as core radiation-protection principles. Limiting unnecessary exposure time and increasing distance reduce dose; appropriate shielding depends on the radiation source and should follow the facility's radiation-safety instructions. Therapeutic radioactive materials also require source-specific contamination controls when applicable. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Radiation exposure is minimized through time, distance, appropriate shielding, and containment; specific shielding/containment must be matched to the radioactive source and radiation-safety program.
candidate.source_document_title: Minimize Your Exposure — Radiation Protection Principles
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'Time, Distance, and Shielding' and 'Containment': limiting exposure time reduces dose; radiation intensity/dose decreases as distance increases; proper shielding reduces penetrating radiation; radioactive materials are contained to limit environmental spread
candidate.stem: A nurse is caring for a hospitalized client who has received therapeutic radioactive material. Which principle should guide the nurse's radiation-safety practices?
